newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Tenaga traces outage to faulty cable.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Tenaga traces outage to faulty cable.

text.p: Malaysia's power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd said it has traced a blackout that struck part of the central business district on Tuesday to a faulty cable.

Tenaga manager of customer relations and media, Syed Hidzam Osman, on Wednesday called the outage a "small incident", which he said affected a few buildings in the so-called 'golden triangle' business area of the capital. He did not have an exact figure for the number of businesses or consumers affected.
Syed Hidzam said a faulty cable at one of the substations supplying power to some buildings caused the blackout at 4.40 p.m. (0840 GMT). Power was restored by 6.25 p.m. (1025 GMT).
"We are still investigating the cause of the faulty cable," he said.
Financial institutions, businesses, hotels and news organisations in the business district were hit by the outage, which happened just ahead of the stock market's trading close at 5 p.m. (0900 GMT).
Traffic was also snarled in some areas as traffic lights failed.
Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) had been preparing to release its financial results for the six months to September 30.
The blackout came as Tenaga was regaining investor and consumer confidence following a 12- to 15-hour nationwide power outage in early August.

Executive Chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali, who took over in September after the massive blackout, spent his first few months reviewing the utility's operations and exploring ways to improve the stability of its power supply.
